2448

         1       relation to nominations for public office.

         2                      ACTING PRESIDENT FARLEY:

         3       Explanation.  Senator Nozzolio.

         4                      SENATOR NOZZOLIO:  This bill

         5       allows a candidate who is nominated by one party

         6       to decline such nomination if that candidate is

         7       hereinafter nominated by that party for another

         8       office.  This happened just this last year with

         9       the eminent Senator to my right, Senator Rath as

        10       an example, who was running for re-election as a

        11       county legislator, was nominated by both the

        12       Republican and Conservative parties.  Upon her

        13       nomination during the special election period to

        14       both parties, that there was a problem in terms

        15       of declination.  This bill would allow that

        16       problem to be eliminated by allowing the

        17       candidate to decline the first nominations even

        18       though it may be nominated by only one of those

        19       two parties.

        20                      ACTING PRESIDENT FARLEY:  Senator

        21       Dollinger.

        22                      SENATOR DOLLINGER:  Will the

        23       sponsor yield to a question just so I make sure











                                                             
2449

         1       I understand this?

         2                      ACTING PRESIDENT FARLEY:  Senator

         3       Nozzolio, will you yield to a question?

         4                      SENATOR NOZZOLIO:  Yes.

         5                      SENATOR DOLLINGER:  Senator, can

         6       you just explain to me the circumstances under

         7       which that works?  You are nominated for a

         8       position by a party, and then there is

         9       subsequently a second nomination at a later time

        10       that requires to you decline, and you are

        11       outside the declination period; is that correct?

        12                      SENATOR NOZZOLIO:  That's

        13       correct, Senator.

        14                      SENATOR DOLLINGER:  So, just so I

        15       understand how it works in the electoral

        16       calendar.  The period, as I recall, in '92 which

        17       is the one I'm most familiar with, there was a

        18       period between the 28th of July and the 3rd of

        19       August, a four- or five-day period in which,

        20       after you were nominated, you could decline the

        21       nomination and take a nomination from another

        22       party.

        23                      SENATOR NOZZOLIO:  Correct,











                                                             
2450

         1       Senator.  That's the normal declination period

         2       traditionally designed so that when some

         3       petitions are filed, then a party has the

         4       opportunity to either accept or decline the

         5       nomination on their behalf.  But when there is

         6       another election taking place, a special

         7       election, where that candidate may be nominated

         8       for a higher office or another office -

         9       obviously the declination period has expired -

        10       because of the changed circumstances, this

        11       would, in effect, inure to the candidate who was

        12       running for another office during the period

        13       after the declination period has been

        14       terminated, is overwith.

        15                      SENATOR DOLLINGER:  Okay.  Thank

        16       you, Mr. President.

        17                      ACTING PRESIDENT FARLEY:  Read

        18       the last section.
